A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same piecewise-guidance research. Their complete text, equations, figures, and end matter support comparison despite substantial reformatting. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: Section V reports original ImageNet restoration experiments, including reconstructed images, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and inference-time comparisons with ΠGDM.

after.justification: Section 5 retains original restoration experiments and adds extended threshold sweeps and a 1,000-image comparison in Table 2.

M1.justification: The two guidance branches, sampling equations, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Theorem 3 adds analytical guidance for selecting T0, without revising the sampler or establishing that this selection rule was used experimentally.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ImageNet images using center-mask and random-mask inpainting, 4× and 8× super-resolution, and conditional/unconditional diffusion models. The additional 1,000-image subset expands sample size within existing coverage.

E2.justification: ΠGDM remains the sole empirically evaluated comparator, including in the new Table 2. Other approaches discussed in related work do not become experimental baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds a separate 1,000-image evaluation at T0=200 alongside the retained 50-image experiments, and extends threshold sweeps from 0–500 to 0–900. Image resolution, degradation operators, metrics, and the 1,000-step diffusion schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing T0 sensitivity analysis extends into higher-threshold regimes. New Figure 11 compares theoretical guidance-error curves across degradation operators. The dog and magpie restoration examples are retained with enlarged displays and zoomed details, rather than constituting new case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. The larger image subset does not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds higher-threshold results and the 1,000-image results in Table 2. For random-mask inpainting, the new table reports ΠGDM versus proposed-method PSNR of 27.73 versus 26.57, LPIPS of 0.10 versus 0.19, and time of 58.2 versus 53.1 seconds. These are additional results under a larger-subset setting; the original curves through T0=500 are retained.

T1.justification: Section 4 corrects the swapped forward-process coefficients in Theorems 1–2 and explicitly conditions the reference distribution on known diffusion noise. It adds an unbiased-denoiser-error assumption, guidance-vector error derivations, and Theorem 3 with a proof of an expected-error criterion for selecting T0.

C1.justification: The problem-agnostic sampling contribution and headline 23–25% time-saving claims remain. V2 removes the separate contribution claiming enhanced real-world noisy-measurement performance through better distribution alignment, while retaining measurement-noise awareness in the general method description.

C2.justification: V2 more explicitly frames the theory as a known-noise idealization and explains that threshold selection depends on the degradation operator and acceptable error. Its experimental discussion shifts from PSNR/SSIM degradation being negligible through T0=500 to broader metric stability, while distinguishing the more noticeable LPIPS degradation.

D1.justification: After Equation 13, v2 newly states that r_t is selected as in the ΠGDM reference. This adds implementation guidance without establishing a changed setting. Hardware specifications and the pretrained-model access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 35 cited works and substantive related-work discussion are retained. A limited positioning change occurs when the contribution list drops the assertion that existing methods often overlook measurement noise; citation-style and bibliographic changes are otherwise presentational.

P1.justification: The six-section narrative and much of the prose remain intact. V2 revises theoretical and experimental explanations, consolidates the contribution list, corrects wording, changes citation and heading styles, and moves the funding acknowledgment into a separate section.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column layout with a single-column format, merges separate conditional/unconditional plots into paired panels, and enlarges restoration examples with zoomed insets. It also relocates the coefficient plot and adds two tables and the theoretical error-curve figure.

improvement.justification: The larger evaluation, extended sensitivity plots, and explicit noise conditioning improve the evidence and clarify v1's theory. However, the new guidance-error formulas omit the variance factor present in Equation 7, and Theorem 3 uses conflicting Frobenius-norm powers in its statement and proof. These inconsistencies undermine the new threshold-selection guarantee, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain despite the empirical additions.
